statement: Q3 results: rolled out VantageScore 4.0 as its preferred model on all eligible loans in September. Coverage of the earnings call shows no discussion of it.

About 2,000 mortgage lenders use VantageScore in underwriting, up sevenfold since April. Most still buy FICO and get VantageScore free; more than 200 use it exclusively. Holds a $1 price through 2028; full conversion worth about $35 million of margin.
Now pulls both scores on every report and automatically uses the stronger result, so brokers no longer choose. Removed its minimum credit score overlays on agency loans.
Credit fees no longer differ by the score model a mortgage is delivered with, for mortgages in MBS issued from October 1.

VantageScore becomes the default in Q4 on eligible direct-to-consumer loans, including GSE and VA. Investment, second-home, FHA, jumbo and home equity loans stay on FICO; Rocket Pro brokers keep both. Tested on 1.4 million reports; borrowers who saved money saved $1,600 on average.
About 25% of its borrowers get a better result with VantageScore, which it says could reach 40%.
Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac move to one pricing grid; separate grids make "zero sense," Director Pulte said.

Reasons lenders hold back: VantageScore's history does not reach the financial crisis, and lenders risk investor buyback requests if loans underperform. TransUnion extended its 99-cent price through 2028.
VantageScore loans at Rocket and UWM, May to August, carried rates about 9.3 bp above comparable FICO loans. The authors cannot identify the driver and say the gap may narrow.
VantageScore was 5.6% of August GSE volume, about 99% of it Rocket and UWM. Most lenders are still pulling FICO scores for almost all loans.
Mortgage insurers' capital rules from September 30 treat a VantageScore loan about like a FICO loan 20 points lower. When a lender submits both scores, the insurer may choose which drives capital.
Not seeing mortgage score volume losses from lenders using VantageScore in addition to FICO. Its Direct License Program was still awaiting certification from one GSE.
A 701 FICO and 760 VantageScore borrower, priced at 740 after the 20-point reduction, saved 75 bp in LLPAs on a $600,000 loan, about $4,500.

AEI estimated the two-score system would cut GSE fee revenue by $1.3 to $1.7 billion a year. Milliman found default rates within the same score cohort about 30% higher under lender choice than under FICO alone.
